bloggers.name: Serenity

posts.text:
$AMD reached out directly to hand me some special swag!

Apparently they only made 30 of these bandanas? 

I love AMD and Lisa Su now. https://t.co/KgcYjBUcTv

I have this feeling that Lisa from $AMD likes AI.

It’s cool getting to meet some of you at the event! https://t.co/AWdGS349xF

Not exactly for $AAOI (they're working on CPO too, just a little further behind in commercialization).

There's a podcast that featured the $SIVE CEO recently called: "Market Insights: Photonics & AI".

Most interesting take was: 

"Pluggables will be around for the next 10 years".

There's a lot of CPO + RNG/MRC optimization TAM cannablization arguments for pluggables recently, but looks like it's here to stay.

And that there's going to be multiple architecture paths going forward (CEO also NPO alongside CPO as an major opportunity in the next 5 years). 

As for challenges: Vickram stated manufacturing capacity + availability of raw material is the main bottleneck. Likely referencing the existing bottlenecks with upstream CW laser ramp. 

From the podcast, seems like a large focus was on pluggable markets due to larger near-term TAM (which is understandable with $JBL + other players), with CPO being the north star. 

So it might be interesting if $SIVE M&A ambitions were to acquire more pluggable optical transceiver IP, like what $LITE did with Cloud Light.

But TLDR:

Lot of different paths moving forward, pluggable here to stay, CPO seems like North Star for where industry is heading. 

Feels like there's room for every qualified laser supplier given the industry demand is growing faster than what they can all collectively make.

From $AMD Advancing AI, channel checks:

Helios networking partners told me they expect AMD to pursue CPO for future generations of Helios scale up networking. 

And expects other hyperscalers + industry to go down the CPO route.

One AI infra executive at a company involved in a hyperscaler CPO programs said they had seen no indication of CPO scale up supply chain delays.

Pushing back on recent 3rd party delay reports.

This was informal commentary, not official AMD or partner guidance.

bloggers.summary:
总体来看，Serenity 对未来 AI 和光互联市场持乐观态度，并对AMD及其CEO Lisa Su表达了高度认可。

- Serenity 对 AMD 表达了积极支持的态度。他提到收到 AMD 的特别赠品并表示喜爱，同时认为 Lisa Su 也很喜欢 AI，这表明他对 AMD 在 AI 领域的发展充满信心。
- - 对于 AMD 和光互联市场（CPO），Serenity 认为未来将有多种架构路径并存，并且 CPO 将是行业发展的北星。态度：看多。他引用了 SIVE CEO 的观点，认为插件式光模块在未来十年内将持续存在。
- - 关于挑战，Serenity 强调制造能力和原材料供应是主要瓶颈。这表明他对 CPO 和相关技术的发展持谨慎乐观的态度。
- - 对于 SIVE 可能的 M&A 活动，Serenity 认为它可能会收购更多插件式光接收器 IP。态度：中性。他提到 AMD 的合作伙伴 Helios 网络预计未来会采用 CPO 技术，并且其他大型云服务商也持相同看法。
- - 从 AMD 在 AI 基础设施方面的进展来看，Serenity 认为市场对 CPO 的需求正在快速增长，而供应链延迟的问题并不严重。态度：看多。他引用了来自一家参与 hyperscaler CPO 项目的公司的高管的评论，认为目前没有大规模供应延迟的迹象。

综上所述，Serenity 对未来 AI 和光互联市场的整体发展持乐观态度，并对 AMD 的发展前景表示认可。

- 期货市场中，菜粕和乙二醇表现强劲，分别录得4.53%和1.83%的涨幅，并吸引大量资金流入。而白银则大幅下跌3.15%，资金流出明显。
- 股市方面，沪深300、中证500与中证1000指数均出现不同程度下跌，但资金流入量较大，分别为54.40亿、41.49亿和41.43亿。碳酸锂则成为资金流出最多的品种，达19.06亿。
- 总体来看，市场情绪有所分化，部分商品期货与股票指数出现显著的资金流入，但也有个别品种如白银面临较大抛压。棕榈油存在卖出信号，需谨慎关注。
